Right to Occupation Indemnity and Calculation of Civil Fruits In a lawsuit for the dissolution of an inheritance community, one co-heir maintained exclusive possession of the inherited residential property, effectively excluding the other heirs from its enjoyment. The legal classification involves the right of co-owners to use common assets (Art. 1102 c.c.) and the accounting of civil fruits (Art. 723 c.c.). The interpretative challenge was whether an heir’s exclusive use of a property triggers an obligation to compensate others in the absence of a formal lease. The Court affirmed that exclusive possession without a valid title constitutes a "loss of use" for the other co-heirs, who are entitled to an "indennità di occupazione." This indemnity is treated as "civil fruits" (frutti civili) and is calculated based on the property's average market rental value from the time a formal demand for release or division was made.
 Judicial Sale of Non-Divisible Property The proceedings also addressed the feasibility of partitioning the estate’s sole apartment among the heirs. The legal issue concerns the criteria for "comoda divisibilità" under Art. 720 c.c.. The interpretative problem arises when a property cannot be split into autonomous units of proportional value without significant depreciation or excessive structural costs. The Court determined that the apartment was physically indivisible due to its size and layout. Since no co-heir formally requested the full attribution of the property with a cash payment to the others, the Court ruled that the asset must be sold through a judicial auction. The proceeds of the sale are then to be distributed among the heirs according to their respective legal shares.
